references.text: The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, which explains why the men of Judah ask the Philistles why they have come up against them.

Samson had previously inflicted great damage on the Philistines by burning their grain fields and killing many of them, which is what the Philistines refer to when they say 'do to him as he has done to us'.
Samson's conflict with the Philistines began here when he killed thirty men from Ashkelon, which is the background for the Philistines' desire for revenge.
The men of Judah actually bind Samson as the Philistines demanded, and handing him over to the enemy is a direct follow-up to this verse.
A similar situation where Israelites were asked to hand over a man to the enemy to avoid conflict.
